summary_md:
**Strongest assumption:** 'zero ungrounded numbers' means fit for a pilot. The guard only checks that a figure matches the metrics table, not that the table is right; categoriser, M13 and M15 were validated only against the project's own generator, which shares their bugs (C8, C12, C17).
**Weakest evidence:** the problem quote is called a 'paraphrase of BridgeTrade broker conversations' here, but lenders-will-pay/bet.md:23 calls the same sentence 'ASSUMPTION, not yet quoted from anyone'. 'Why now' cites no burned lender. Tier: opinion. The only test-tier evidence is negative (panel FAIL, C1–C6).
**Pre-mortem 1:** no statement arrives by week 6. Anonymised SME statements are still personal data for sole traders; free outreach with no sponsor and no DPA stalls in the lender's compliance team.
**Pre-mortem 2:** a statement arrives as a PDF or bank export, real acquirer descriptors fall to 'other' (revenue near £0), redacted payer names break M15, the VAT rule refers compliant businesses, and the memo is 'grounded' but wrong, which burns the first real analyst.
**Scope:** kill criterion 2 is a demand test that duplicates lenders-will-pay; the outcome has no correctness baseline (no analyst spread of the same statement to compare against) and 'week 6' has no start date.

questions.context: Where did the problem quote come from? This bet calls it a paraphrase of BridgeTrade broker conversations; lenders-will-pay/bet.md:23 says it is an assumption not yet quoted from anyone. To settle it, produce the dated notes or run one new interview. Recalling it from memory does not count as evidence.
options: Dated notes exist with at least one broker saying something close to it
Owner remembers conversations but has no notes
It is a composite the owner wrote; no one said it
Don't know

questions.context: What file will a pilot lender actually send? v0.1 reads only the synthetic five-column CSV (id, date, description, amount, balance), and CAMT/MT940 adapters are a non-goal. To find out, ask three contacts to describe or send a redacted sample of what their analysts receive today.
options: A CSV export that maps cleanly to the v0.1 schema
Bank PDF statements (needs OCR or extraction before ingest)
Open Banking or aggregator JSON (Plaid/TrueLayer/Codat)
The lender's own spread spreadsheet, not raw lines
Don't know

questions.context: Who anonymises the statement, under what data-protection basis, and does the anonymised data still work? A sole trader's statement is personal data even with the name removed. Redacting payer names breaks M15 and the FPS CREDIT categoriser rules. Test this by running one redacted statement the way the lender would redact it and see which metrics survive.
options: Lender redacts names and shares under a short data-processing agreement
Owner receives raw data and anonymises it (owner becomes a processor; needs a DPA and secure handling)
Lender runs v0.1 inside its own environment; no data leaves
Owner builds a synthetic lookalike from the lender's description of a real case
Don't know

questions.context: Outcome and baseline: the success measure is 'zero ungrounded numbers', but a number can be grounded and still wrong. Is there an existing analyst spread of the same statement to compare metrics against, and what tolerance counts as a match? Getting this needs a data request to the pilot lender.
options: Yes: the analyst's existing spread is available and each metric must match within an agreed tolerance
No spread exists; the analyst will judge qualitatively
Grounding alone is the bar for v0.1; correctness is v0.2
Don't know

questions.context: Who, by name, would run the statement? Is there anyone who has said yes in principle, and when does the 'week 6' kill clock start? The playbook has outreach in week 3, and C1–C6 still need fixing first. Check this against the outreach log, not memory.
options: At least one named analyst or broker has agreed in writing
Warm contacts exist from BridgeTrade but none has been asked about this
No current contact; cold NACFB list only
Don't know

questions.context: Why now: is there evidence that UK lenders are actually trialling LLM memo tools and getting burned by invented figures? And would the differentiator survive if Ocrolus, Codat or Plaid ship cited memos (Plaid launched LendScore 2 on 6 Oct 2026)? Answering needs a source search or three interview questions.
options: A public incident or report names this failure at a UK lender
One or more contacts described it first-hand
Owner's inference from general LLM hallucination coverage
Don't know

questions.context: Scope of this bet: kill criterion 2 ('no lender or broker agrees to run a statement by week 6') tests demand and overlaps lenders-will-pay. As written, an engineering bet can be killed by a sales outcome, and its own engineering fitness has no pass date.
options: Keep both criteria here
Move criterion 2 to lenders-will-pay; replace with 'C1–C6 fixed and panel run 02 passes R2, R4, R5, R9 by a fixed date'
Add a correctness criterion against real-format descriptors (e.g. revenue within 2% on a hand-built real-format statement) alongside the panel re-run
Don't know

proposals.text: Keep confidence at 'opinion'. The problem statement is an unsourced paraphrase that a sibling bet calls an assumption. 'Why now' cites no instance. The only test-tier evidence (the six-seat panel run) is negative. Raise to 'anecdote' only with dated notes from a named broker, and to 'test' only after one external-format statement has been run and compared against an analyst's spread.
